author: Mike Hanks
title: Bloomington man charged with criminal sexual conduct involving teen - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Hanks ,
13 hours ago A 24-year-old Bloomington man has been charged with two counts of criminal sexual conduct involving a juvenile.
The suspect was charged March 25 in Hennepin County District Court with one second-degree count and one third-degree count. If convicted on the second-degree charge, he faces up to 25 years in prison and a fine between $10,500 and $35,000. If convicted on the third-degree charge, he faces up to five years in prison and a fine between $10,000 and $30,000, plus conditional release.
The suspect is accused of having sex with a 15-year-old Shakopee girl at his Bloomington apartment in January. The investigation originated in Shakopee, and Shakopee Police Department investigators provided details of their reports to Bloomington investigators in early February, according to Bloomington Police Cmdr. Eric Kittelson.
The investigation began when the 15-year-old girl’s father found that she had three cellphones, two of which he did not know she had. He found videos on at least one of the phones that included male nudity and other explicit images. The father turned them over to the Shakopee Police Department. Investigators examining the images and videos on the phone determined some of the explicit images were of the 15-year-old girl, Kittelson said.
When questioned about the phones, the girl identified the suspect as the source of one of the phones. She said she met him by communicating through the Snapchat multimedia messaging platform, had snuck out of her house and had sex with the suspect at his Bloomington apartment. She said the suspect knew she was 15 when they began corresponding, Kittelson noted.
The girl reported that the suspect initially said he was 17 through Snapchat communication, but after they met, he said he was 19 years old, and he instructed the girl not to tell anyone about their relationship, the criminal complaint explained.
The investigation showed that a Snapchat account used to communicate with the girl had the same phone number that the suspect gave to the victim, and was used to confirm his identity, the complaint noted.
The girl said that she last saw the suspect on Jan. 24. She said she had snuck out of her house the previous night, and that the suspect picked her up. They went to the suspect’s apartment, where the suspect allegedly gave the girl alcohol and had sex with her. When the suspect determined the girl needed to leave his apartment, she was intoxicated, so the suspect helped her get dressed, the complaint explained.
After helping her to his car, the suspect drove her home, but they stopped at a convenience store along the way, as the girl needed to use a restroom. While in the restroom, she took a video of herself. Investigators found the video on one of the girl’s cellphones, and were able to match her to store surveillance video from approximately 5 a.m. Jan. 24. A male who appeared to match the suspect also appeared in surveillance videos, which showed the duo interacting inside the store. Parking lot surveillance footage showed a 2012 Toyota Corolla in the parking lot, which is registered to the suspect, the complaint noted.
The girl provided a sketch and description of the suspect’s apartment and said that she had sex with the suspect each time they were together. A search warrant for the suspect’s Snapchat account showed communication between him and the girl, who referenced being in high school, with the girl professing that she loved the suspect. Explicit images and images showing the suspect’s apartment, including red LED lighting the girl described, were found in his account, according to the complaint.
A search warrant executed at his apartment on March 24 resulted in his arrest, the complaint noted.
End of staycation
A 42-year-old Minneapolis man was charged with two misdemeanor counts of domestic assault following a report that he assaulted a 35-year-old woman at a Bloomington hotel.
Police officers were dispatched to La Quinta Inn, 7815 Nicollet Ave., at approximately 7:40 p.m. March 20 in response to a report that the Minneapolis woman had been assaulted in a hotel room. The woman told officers that the suspect is her boyfriend and that they had been arguing in their hotel room, according to the criminal complaint.
During the argument, the suspect allegedly grabbed her by the throat and began to choke her. She was having difficulty breathing when he threw her onto the floor by her neck, grabbed her head and hit her face against the floor, which caused her nose to bleed. When the woman threatened to call 911, the suspect left the room, the complaint explained.
The woman said she feared for her safety, prompting her to call 911. The officers who spoke with her at the hotel noted that she had a swollen nose, a scratch on her neck and blood on her hand, which she said was from wiping blood from her nose, the complaint noted.
The suspect had remained at the hotel and was arrested on suspicion of domestic assault. Following his arrest, he told officers that his girlfriend initiated the confrontation during their argument, and that he held her down on the floor to keep her from getting physical with him. He suggested that she hit her head on a table while he was attempting to hold her down, according to the complaint.
He also claimed that his girlfriend’s actions were a result of her use of drugs and alcohol, Kittelson noted.
If convicted of causing fear or inflicting bodily harm, he faces up to 90 days in jail and a fine of up to $1,000 for each count.
Missed departure leads to jail
A domestic dispute between a 30-year-old Eden Prairie man and his girlfriend ended with his arrest in the parking lot of the Bloomington Walmart store.
The suspect was arrested shortly after noon March 23 after both he and his 31-year-old girlfriend reported that they had been fighting in his vehicle after she missed a flight at the Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport.
The fight ended when the suspect pulled into the Walmart parking lot, where the woman exited his vehicle. She went inside the store and found an off-duty police officer working at the store and reported that she was assaulted by the suspect, according to Kittelson.
She said that her boyfriend picked her up at the airport after she missed a flight, and as they were arguing about her missed flight, he allegedly punched her in the face before pulling over. She said he then pulled her out of the vehicle and struck her again. She had swelling and a cut near her eye as she gave her report, Kittelson said.
After he pulled into Walmart and she exited his vehicle, the suspect called 911 to report that his girlfriend allegedly began punching him while he was driving, nearly causing an accident. He said that when he pulled over, he only told her to exit his vehicle. Although he claimed self defense, he said he may have struck his girlfriend in the face as he was trying to stop her from hitting him, Kittelson explained.
The suspect was booked on suspicion of felony domestic assault and Hennepin County declined to charge him in custody, Kittelson noted.
